result.title: Keyline Detection with YOLO: Runway Perception for Vision-Based Aircraft Landing
result.summary: Modern object detectors can predict keypoints as per-object geometric features, but keypoints are inherently vulnerable to occlusion and truncation. Object edges can provide complementary information, often remaining observable even when partially occluded or when their defining endpoints leave the field of view. We therefore introduce object keyline detection, the task of predicting a fixed, semantically ordered set of infinite lines per object instance. Unlike the outputs of general line-segment detectors, each keyline is associated with an object instance and identified by a semantic index, providing a line-level analog of keypoints. To solve this task, we extend YOLO with keyline prediction parameterized in continuous Hesse-normal form $[ρ,\cosθ,\sinθ]$, and introduce Object Keyline Similarity (OKLS), which serves as an evaluation metric, target assignment signal, and regression loss. We instantiate this formulation on runway perception in vision-based landing, a motivating example containing semantic linear features that remain partially observable throughout the approach. Experiments show that our representation achieves the highest detection accuracy among four evaluated line parameterizations, and keylines integrate directly into standard YOLO heads as additional output channels without degrading keypoint performance or adding meaningful latency.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 object keyline detection 任务：为每个目标实例预测一组固定且语义有序的无限直线，将 YOLO 扩展为以 Hesse 法式 [ρ, cosθ, sinθ] 连续参数回归 keyline，并提出 OKLS 同时用作评价指标、目标分配信号与回归损失，在基于视觉的着陆跑道感知上验证。
AI.relevance_reason: 与 LVR 主线无直接关联（纯视觉检测、不涉及 VLM 或 latent 推理），但其用语义索引化的线状几何表示替代易受遮挡的关键点，并让同一相似度兼作损失与分配信号，可能为内部状态中保留任务必要的几何证据及相应监督设计提供可供核查的线索。
